name: The Bomb Squad
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 boom-bap — The Bomb Squad
Reverb — the production of Public Enemy: gear, sampling and embracing distortion (https://reverb.com/news/the-production-of-public-enemy-gear-sampling-and-embracing-distortion)
notes: Windowed to 1990–1991 (Fear of a Black Planet, Apocalypse 91) per the research's era gate; the 1987–89 material is out of scope. Three parameters carry it and every one is documented. First, tempo: 100–112 is the fastest band on this axis by a clear margin, and it is why the kit reads as clatter rather than as a break. Second, key: "atonal-leaning by design — dozens of layered fragments in different keys, so harmony is a noise-band rather than a chord", which is all twelve keys at equal weight with `chromatic` leading the scale set — no other entry on this axis has a chromatic scale — plus `halfStepDissonance` 0.35 and `chordToneBias` 0.35, the lowest here. Third, the collage: motifs "1 bar or less, changing every 4–8 bars" is `phraseBars` [1,2] weighted 4:2 with `leap` at 0.4, and "layers added and removed every 4 bars" is `switchUpProb` 0.55 with a 0.7 drop-out. The 16th hat/percussion clatter is `fillDensity` 0.8 over seven perc lanes at 4–9 hits a bar. ⚠ Where a tonic exists the research says it is a funk i7, so `extensions.seventh` is 0.7 and `impliedByRiff` is set — there are no loops here in the conventional sense, so there is no progression to write. ⚠ `medium` because the research rates it high-medium: the production philosophy and the distortion approach are first-person across multiple interviews, the drum probabilities are not. The specific inferred parameter is `kick.syncopation` at 0.7 — "kick on 1, 2.5 and 3.5" gives positions, not a rate. ⚠ The i–iv and i–VII families are INFERRED and carry the lowest weights; the research names no progression at all. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [49, 89] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 40 against a bass reaching 48, an overlap of 9. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ `countermelody.fillGapsOnly` returned to true. With it off and a density of 0.7, the counter plays THROUGH the melody rather than around it, and coherence.rs measures that as the counter sounding the melody own pitch at the same moment — a second lead rather than an answer. The register offset and the styles are untouched; what changed is that it waits its turn. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
